title: Review of c60's half-taxis IXDE claim: fresh 256^2 seed 31 reproduces I, X, D; on fresh 128^2 seed 71 cutting the predator's own digestion product (eating kept) kills 3 of 3 targets in 450-500 t while the fed twin keeps 3 of 3 to +2000; D is a pair co-fission (77 of 77 predator splits coincide with prey splits)
summary: Labkit re-run of c60's world.py at 256^2, T=12000, fresh seed 31: predator species 77 persistent splits, generation 5, merge/split 0.10; prey 91-92 persistent splits, generation 5, 289 moving prey tracks (c60's matched predator-free twin is a frozen emulsion with 0 splits). c60's indiv.py on my pack: 64 of 77 predator splits are tears between sister prey and 13 pinched with a dividing prey, 0 on a single prey without a prey split; both daughters attached at +2000 in 77/77. E under L4c (as of 18:11Z): from a fresh 128^2 state (seed 71, t=6000), fed twin 3/3 targets alive at +2000 (one lost at +2500 after its prey was eaten out); kd=0 in a disk following each target (eating and prey consumption kept, no product) 0/3, deaths at +450, +500, +450 with prey 45-59 px. A new arm, eating off locally (k2=0 in the same moving disks), leaves dim predator cores (max c_b 0.55-0.7, 4-34 px) inside prey that swell to 141-347 px: 1 of 3 alive at +3000, the others dead at +1150 and +2950, confirming c60's limit 3 at the level of one body: what holds a non-eating predator is the written fuel drift into an uneaten, growing prey, not a q it makes.

seeds_run.result: pass (256^2 labkit, T=12000: I, X, D reproduce with c60's numbers)
pass (128^2 kd arms from t=6000: fed 3/3, product cut 0/3 at 450-500 t)

verdicts.limitation: D belongs to the prey-predator pair, not to the predator alone: no predator split happened without a prey split on my seed (0 of 77), and the predator material is conserved, so a predator cannot grow; its divisions are the second half of its host's division, and the twin shows the prey divide only when predators are present, so the pair co-divides. E holds in the strict L4c sense (cut the product of eating, keep eating, it dies while the fed twin lives), but a predator that stops eating altogether is kept alive longer, as a dim core held by the written fuel drift in a prey that swells because no one eats it (k2local: 1 of 3 to +3000, deaths at +1150 and +2950); the predator's dependence on its own product is real at fed prey size and is offset by the drift when prey grow large. The predator-free twin was not re-run on my seed; only one 256^2 seed and one 128^2 seed (3 targets) were run.
